relationship: Programming rover commands and their Huffman codes connects a route's command frequencies to encoded transmission length.

learnerLoop.action: Build a rover program, edit its command codes and run the decoded transmission.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The command sequence, bit count and rover position change.
learnerLoop.evidence: The map, bit tape, score and codebook show the transmitted result.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Revise the route or code lengths to reach the goal with fewer bits.

invariants: The bit count follows the current commands and their codes.
Running the transmission moves the rover according to the decoded command sequence.
safeAdaptations: Change map layouts, route goals or starter programs while preserving command coding and bit-cost feedback.
nonGoals: Teaching a complete compression file format or arbitrary prefix-code implementation.

task.description: Reach the beacon with the shortest valid transmission.
task.visibility: Visible in the corresponding editing, simulation or result state.

controls.description: Append commands, edit prefix codes, reset and run the decoder.
controls.visibility: Visible in the corresponding editing, simulation or result state.

model.description: Fixed obstacle map, programmed route and consuming bitstream.
model.visibility: Visible in the corresponding editing, simulation or result state.

evidence.description: Prefix validity, command frequencies, route cost and actual decoded outcome.
evidence.visibility: Visible in the corresponding editing, simulation or result state.

codes.domain: Four nonempty prefix-free binary strings, each field limited to six characters.

cost.domain: Sum of code lengths over the programmed route; valid routes compared against fixed 19-bit mission optimum.

modes.editing: Program and codebook can be edited until execution begins.
modes.execution: Bitwise decoding; each complete code turns and moves the rover one square.

dependencies: Route simulation determines whether cost can be scored; actual execution still shows obstacles.
Reset rover cancels a run; starter route restores the supplied program.
Model artwork and command meanings are retained. Shared hints introduce execution, command entry and codebook editing.
implementation.completion: Execution ends at an obstacle, after consuming the stream, or at the beacon; score compares valid routes with the fixed optimum.
limitations: This is a fixed mission with a stated optimum, not a general-purpose Huffman-tree builder.
